descriptions.server/context_schema.py: A data structure that stores metadata about conversation turns and messages—information about when something happened, who said it, what role they had, what they were doing, and when the information expires. It normalizes messy metadata into a clean, consistent format with fields for agent name, speaker role, source system, turn number, tags, timestamps, and time-to-live expiration days. It handles various input formats like timestamps as strings or date objects, tags as lists or individual strings, and converts them all to standard representations. Input is raw metadata dictionaries or dataclass objects, output is normalized, serializable dictionaries with proper types and expiration calculations. The module is purely for defining and converting metadata structures rather than doing runtime work.
descriptions.server/models.py: This file defines Pydantic data models representing the contract for a vector search and context storage system. It includes models for context items with optional IDs and metadata, batch operations adding multiple items to a session, search requests with query text and filtering options, search results returning scored hits with metadata, session management showing document counts and time ranges, and utility models for health checks and dashboard summaries. The models use type hints and field descriptions to enable validation and documentation of request/response payloads, particularly for an HTTP API serving knowledge retrieval and session management.
descriptions.server/store.py: This wraps ChromaDB (a vector database) to store documents as searchable embeddings organized into session collections—like a library where you can search for documents by meaning rather than just keywords. The VectorStore class manages a persistent ChromaDB client, provides methods to add items (documents with metadata), search by semantic similarity with optional keyword bonuses, and explore what's stored. When adding items, it generates unique IDs and normalizes metadata. Search converts ChromaDB's distance metric into similarity scores (0 to 1), accounting for whether the distance is cosine, inner product, or squared L2 (ChromaDB's default). It returns ranked hits with scores and metadata. Additional methods list sessions, get statistics, prune expired entries by timestamp, and dump complete session contents. Input is text documents with metadata tags; output is ranked search results with similarity scores. The store handles distance metric conversions transparently so callers see consistent similarity scores regardless of the collection's internal distance space.
descriptions.server/store_api.py: This file provides a thin wrapper around a remote vector database API, presenting an HTTP interface to a FastAPI server on localhost:8765 as if it were a local vector database object. It mirrors the embedded vector database interface so callers can use the same method names (add_items, search, session_stats, prune_expired, etc.) without knowing whether the data is being stored locally or on a remote server. The VectorStore class takes an optional API base URL (defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8765 from environment variable AIONS_API_BASE_URL) and makes HTTP POST or GET requests for every operation: adding items to a session, searching a session with a query and optional metadata filters, listing sessions, checking health, pruning expired records, getting a dashboard summary, and retrieving status. All network requests wrap errors into RuntimeError exceptions so callers know if something went wrong without needing to handle HTTP-specific exceptions. Someone integrating a vector database server into a system that needs to run in multiple places, separating the database layer from application code, or wanting to query AIONS data from outside processes would use this API client.
descriptions.server/store_http.py: This file implements the vector storage backend using ChromaDB with two connection modes: HTTP (connecting to a remote server) or embedded (local storage). It tries first to connect via HTTP to a ChromaDB server on 127.0.0.1:8000, falling back to embedded mode if the server is down. Collections are created per session, keeping documents and their metadata organized. When you search, it converts Chroma's distance scores to similarity scores (0 to 1) accounting for the actual distance metric used (L2, cosine, inner product). It handles keyword boosting to increase scores for documents matching all query words. The store tracks which mode it's using and logs degraded-to-embedded failures to a runtime log. It can reconnect to HTTP mode later if the server comes back online.
descriptions.server/store_selector.py: This file automatically chooses which vector database backend to use—HTTP or embedded—based on environment configuration or automatic detection. If the CHROMA_USE_HTTP environment variable is explicitly set to 'true', it loads the HTTP implementation; if set to 'false', it loads the embedded implementation; otherwise it tries to connect to an HTTP ChromaDB server by making a heartbeat call to test availability, falling back to embedded if that fails. The file re-exports the VectorStore class and get_connection_mode function from whichever backend was selected. It takes no input data directly but reads environment variables CHROMA_USE_HTTP, CHROMA_HOST, and CHROMA_PORT. The output is transparently swapped imports so the rest of the application always imports from this module regardless of which backend is active. It talks to the chromadb library to test HTTP connectivity. Someone would ask about this when they want their application to automatically work with either a remote shared ChromaDB server or a local copy depending on what's available.
